result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of the name is. The `*Scoping*` tests in `codeanalyzer` pass. I didn't add new test cases for the new folder shapes, and I didn't run the other modules' tests.

**Change:** in `addTestConventions` in `ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), I replaced the character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+` with `[^/\\\\]*` in the `__mock…` and `mock…` rules. The rest of the name can now be anything except a slash or backslash, including nothing at all. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and non-ASCII names like `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`.

**Why it stays in one folder name:** the rule still needs a `/` before `mock`, so `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match. Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match either, because the rule needs a `/` after the folder name.

**Windows paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries a backslash-to-slash version of the path, so backslash paths work without further changes.

The old name shapes (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) are all matched by the new pattern too. I reasoned that from the regex rather than running those exact names through it.
